# Rule inferred from the data: a non-initial schwa [ə] is written "’" only when
# the following consonant is an obstruent. Before a sonorant (m, n, l) it is
# left unwritten. Long vowels are also written with "’" after the vowel.
# Each tuple is (word, following consonant, whether the schwa is written as ’).
obs = [
    ("tmi’gn  dəm", "m", False),
    ("tmi’gn  gən", "n", False),
    ("an’stawteg nəs", "s", True),
    ("mgumie’jo’tlatl dəl", "l", False),
    ("mgumie’jo’tlatl adəl", "l", False),
    ("e’jnt jən", "n", False),
    ("tplutaqan pəl", "l", False),
    ("lnu’sgw lən", "n", False),
    ("g’p’ta’q gəb", "b", True),
    ("g’p’ta’q bəd", "d", True),
]
sonorants = set("mnl")

def predict_written(next_c):
    return next_c not in sonorants

ok = True
for name, c, written in obs:
    p = predict_written(c)
    print(name, "next:", c, "observed written:", written, "predicted:", p)
    if p != written:
        ok = False
print("rule consistent with all data:", ok)

# Target: [alaptək] -> a l a p t ə k; the schwa is before k (an obstruent).
next_c = "k"
written = predict_written(next_c)
derived = "alapt" + ("’" if written else "") + "k"
print("derived:", derived)
submitted = "alapt’k"
print("submitted:", submitted)
if ok and derived == submitted:
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")
